title: Plain text line
description: The Case text followed by one LF. The baseline carrier; every authored Case with input text is in scope, whatever its role or identity state, because the expectation is copied as authored.

expectation.basis: Plain text line is representational only: the authored Case text, label and value bytes are carried through unchanged, so the semantic outcome stated by the Case is expected to hold. This equivalence is project inference, unreviewed; it is the rule author's assumption and is not scanner-corroborated.

title: JSON object field
description: The Case text as the JSON string value of one field of a single-line object. Characters are escaped per JSON string rules; a Case whose value would be altered by escaping is skipped, never rewritten.

expectation.basis: JSON object field is representational only: the authored Case text, label and value bytes are carried through unchanged, so the semantic outcome stated by the Case is expected to hold. This equivalence is project inference, unreviewed; it is the rule author's assumption and is not scanner-corroborated.

title: logfmt key-value line
description: The Case text as a double-quoted logfmt value after a fixed level key. Backslash, double quote and line breaks are escaped; a Case whose value would be altered is skipped.

expectation.basis: logfmt key-value line is representational only: the authored Case text, label and value bytes are carried through unchanged, so the semantic outcome stated by the Case is expected to hold. title: Form or query string field
description: The Case text as one percent-encoded query or form field. Only bytes outside unreserved characters and the safe punctuation set are encoded (space becomes %20). Restricted to shape-identified kinds without contexts, because label-dependent kinds lose their label cue when its punctuation is encoded; a Case whose value would be altered by encoding is skipped.

expectation.basis: Form or query string field is representational only: the authored Case text, label and value bytes are carried through unchanged, so the semantic outcome stated by the Case is expected to hold. This equivalence is project inference, unreviewed; it is the rule author's assumption and is not scanner-corroborated.

title: Multibyte label prefix
description: A fixed multibyte (Korean) label placed before the Case text, shifting every byte offset. Justified by the authored Case that already records an email after a multibyte label; limited to the email kind for that reason.
